This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
The above appeal is filed by the insurer challenging the judgment and award dated 22.6.2015 passed
in Mvc No.202/2014 by the Senior Civil Judge and Additional Mact, Holalkere1.
2.
For the sake of conv
enience, the parties herein are referred as per their rank before the Tribunal.
3. The Tribunal by its judgment and award dated 22.6.2015 awarded a sum of `4,55,000/- together with interest at 8% pa., from the date of petition till date of payment.
Being aggrieved, the insurer has filed the above appeal alleging that the quantum of compensation awarded is on the higher side.
The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal on negligence and quantum are not under challenge.
Hence, the only question that is required to be considered in the present appeal is whether the quantum of compensation awarded is excessive.
Hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal' NC: 2024:KHC:6749 4.
The claimant was aged 22 years as on the date of the accident i.e., on 1.12.2013.
Hence, the appropriate multiplier is 18 as has been assessed by the Tribunal.
5. The claimant is stated to be driver of paddy cutting machine and also engaged in agricultural activities.
However, no documents have been produced to prove his income.
The Tribunal has assessed the income as `6,500/- pm.

Having regard to the fact that the claimant has not produced any document to prove his income, the same is required to be reassessed as per the chart followed for settlement of claims in Lok Adalath conducted by Legal Services Authority and having regard to the date of accident i.e., 1.12.2013 the income is reassessed as `8,000/- pm.

6. It is forthcoming from the wound certificate (Ex.P3), disability certificate (Ex.P6) and the disability certificate (Ex.P11) as well as the testimony of the doctor who has been examined as PW.2 that the claimant sustained fracture of the shoulder joint as well as the comminuted fracture of the shaft of the left humorous.
The claimant has taken treatment as an inpatient for 10 days.
The doctor has NC: 2024:KHC:6749 assessed the functional disability as 35%.

However, the Tribunal,
reassessing the same has assessed the whole body disability as 10%.

2 7.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant - insurer assailing the finding of the Tribunal regarding disability submits that the doctor - PW.2 is not the treated doctor and the disability mentioned by the said doctor as well as in the disability certificate (Ex.P11) is excessive.
8. It is noticed that the claimant has sustained fracture of left shoulder joint and left humorous.
The said fractures have been surgically treated.
Subsequent to the discharge, he has also taken treatment as an outpatient.

Although the doctor has stated with regard to restriction in the movement of the left arm, having regard to the nature of injuries and the resultant disability, it is just and proper that the functional disability to the whole body be reassessed as 8%.

9. In view of the aforementioned, the compensation is reassessed as follows:
NC: 2024:KHC:6749 9.1

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of `1,00,000/-
towards pain and suffering, which is excessive.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained and the period of treatment, it is just and proper that the compensation be reassessed as `30,000/-.
9.2 The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `50,000/- towards medical and incidental expenses.
It is forthcoming that the bills produced as Exs.P8 an P9 are for a sum of `39,000/-.
Hence, it is just and proper to reassess the medical expenses at `40,000/-.

9.3 Having regard to the nature of injuries and the period for which the claimant was treated as an inpatient, it is just and proper to award a sum of `20,000/- towards food, nutrition, attendant charges and conveyance.
9.4 The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `50,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Having regard to the nature of injuries and the resultant disability, it is just and proper that the same be reassessed as `20,000/-.

9.5 Having regard to the nature of injuries and the period of treatment, the laid up period is taken as 3 months NC: 2024:KHC:6749 and the loss of income during laid up period is reassessed as (`8000/-x3) `24,000/-.
9.6

Loss of future income is reassessed as (`8000x x12x18x8%) `1,38,240/- as against `1,40,400/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

9.7 The compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards permanent disability, future prospects,
future expenses and cost of litigation are set aside.

10. Accordingly, the total compensation under various heads is reassessed as follows:
